title: Saving Early for College
learningObjectives: Understand how time and compound interest can increase savings
Understand the value of starting early to save for post-secondary education

evidence.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

explanations.text: Compound interest means you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you have already earned.

evidence.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).

explanations.text: The example starts with a $1,000 principal earning 5 percent compounded once a year.

evidence.quote: After the first year, you would have $1,050—your original principal, plus 5 percent, or $50.
The second year, you would have $1,102.50.

explanations.text: That savings grows to $1,050 after the first year and to $1,102.50 in the second year.

evidence.quote: The sooner you start saving for post-secondary education, the faster your money can grow from compound interest.
Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.

explanations.text: Starting to save early for post-secondary education helps money grow, and raising the frequency, rate, or principal can make it grow even faster.
